- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 2–5 day lag correction after a +5%+ price surge.
- Forecast mean reverts to 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days; use this as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overshoots early in the forecast; cap forecast at 10% above 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment and price history show divergence (e.g., sentiment up but price falling), model overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–7 days.
